plan.title: 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DE in brain RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than WT — is formally the genotype:treatment interaction term in a 2x2 factorial design (WT/KO x vehicle/drug, n=4/cell, 12000 genes, 16 samples per metadata; counts.csv has 17 columns because one is the gene symbol column). The plan follows the DESeq2 interaction workflow: (1) QC on sample structure to catch outliers/batch before modeling, (2) minimal count pre-filtering, (3) fit the full model genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment with explicit reference levels (WT, vehicle), (4) test the interaction coefficient first (the formal answer to 'does drug act differently by genotype') via Wald test, then decompose into simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT; drug vs vehicle within KO) to characterize the direction/magnitude of the differential response, (5) shrink fold changes (apeglm for single coefficients, ashr for the simple-effect contrasts), (6) BH-adjust at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, (7) run preranked fgsea against MSigDB Hallmark on the interaction and simple-effect statistics to interpret which pathways show genotype-dependent drug response, (8) integrate into one report stating the low power inherent to n=4/cell for interaction detection and all reporting requirements (versions, design, thresholds, N tested/DE, session info). A cross-check with edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design is included as the recommended second method for a high-confidence intersection set, since interaction calls at n=4 are noisy.

apeglm for single coefficients (main effects, interaction coefficient); ashr for simple-effect contrasts not equal to a model coefficient
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic vs MSigDB Hallmark (human)
Integrated DE + interaction + enrichment report with session info and versions
